scope: Theorem 1.2 (Global application) of the manuscript “Single-exponential recovery and bounded-price strictness for metric k-median” (preprints/Single-Exponential-Recovery-and-Bounded-Price-Strictness-for-Metric-k-Median-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 125 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 823fdb284a7d3c0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 3-4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant σ > 0 with the following property. For every fixed a > 0, a randomized polynomial-time algorithm for metric k-median always returns a set S ⊆ F with |S| ≤ k and satisfies Pr{cost(S) ≤ (2 − σ) optk} ≥ 1 − (|D| + |F| + 2)−a . 3 The same algorithm can be chosen to satisfy E cost(S) ≤ (2 − σ) optk. The running time is poly- nomial in the bit length of the finite rational metric input. Its degree may depend on the fixed constants.
